verifier_note: Retrieved all 46 primary warrant sources by direct fetch (std docs on doc.rust-lang.org incl. the 1.80.0 archived slice page, the Book, the Reference, 2 error_codes pages, 3 GitHub PRs, RELEASES.md at tag 1.98.1, and 5 rapier3d-f64 0.35.3 docs.rs source files), using raw-HTML curl+grep instead of WebFetch's summarizer wherever a page was large enough to get truncated (Vec, slice, f64, char). Ran every one of the lane's 30 checks myself through scripts/compile_oracle.py against the real pinned rustc 1.98.1: 30/30 passed verbatim, including implementation-specific numbers (sort_by_key 1406 key calls vs sort_by_cached_key 100; sort_unstable_by ties held at n=20 but broke at n=21/100; binary_search([1,2,2,2,3],2)=Ok(3); char::UNICODE_VERSION=(17,0,0); the stable-vs-unstable differential panic behavior on a lying comparator). Checked all 7 engine_note claims against si-rpg-engine's live main via gh api (rapier_law.rs 772 lines, lib.rs 307 lines, Cargo.toml): rebuild_snapshot's out.clear()+pairs.sort_by on (collider1,collider2).into_raw_parts(), canon()'s -0.0-to-+0.0 fold, canon_quat's NaN-to-None, mix_f64's uncanonicalized to_bits(), BODY_STRIDE=17/COLLIDER_STRIDE=10, the zero HashMap/BTreeMap grep hits, and edition="2021" all matched exactly. No source misattribution, no stale API, no wrong engine fact, and no check that tested something other than its recipe's prose. Systemic weakness: a few one-sentence gotchas ride on a sibling check rather than getting their own — recipe 6's "for e in [1, 2, 3] iterates by value in every edition" is not exercised by any of its 5 checks (they test explicit .into_iter() calls, not the bare-literal for-loop desugaring), and recipe 3's "entry(key) moves a String key even when already present" is asserted from the entry(key: K) signature alone with no compile_fail demonstrating the moved-value error. I independently wrote and ran a counter-example for the first (edition 2018/2015, `for x in [1,2,3] { let y: i32 = x; }` compiles, proving by-value iteration) and it held; the second follows deductively from the confirmed by-value signature. A reader who trusted only checks[] as ground truth would not catch a regression in either claim.
